days.title: Arrive in Grindelwald
days.description: Base of operations under the Eiger north face

activities.activity: Train transfer from Zurich and check-in below the north face
activities.notes: Meet your IFMGA guide for route briefing and the first look at the forecast

activities.activity: Gear check: rack, ropes, crampons, axes, helmet

days.title: Warm-up on the Schwarzhorn
days.description: Shake out the travel legs on moving-together terrain

activities.activity: Climb the Schwarzhorn west ridge (F+/PD) for acclimatisation
activities.notes: 2,928 m — a fast rock ridge to calibrate pace and rope work with your partner
3,454 m — take it slow on arrival, altitude is real up here

activities.activity: Crevasse-rescue and short-roping refresher on the Jungfraufirn
activities.notes: Europe's highest serviced hut at 3,657 m — early night before the first objective

activities.activity: Climb the Mönch southeast ridge (AD, mixed snow and rock)
activities.notes: 4,107 m — exposed snow crest to finish; turn around by 11:00 if the window closes

days.title: Descend and recover in the valley
days.description: Planned rest before the main event

activities.activity: Train down from Jungfraujoch and easy valley afternoon
activities.notes: Rest day — massage, sort photos, study the Mittellegi topo over coffee

activities.activity: Check the weather window and avalanche/serac conditions with the guide office
activities.notes: Go/no-go decision point — the ridge needs a dry 36-hour window

activities.activity: Train to Eismeer station and climb the fixed-rope access to the hut
activities.notes: 3,355 m eyrie on the ridge itself — one of the great hut positions in the Alps

activities.activity: Climb the Mittellegi ridge (D, sustained exposure, fixed ropes on the steep step)
activities.notes: 3,967 m — 10 to 12 hours summit-to-safety; abseils down the south ridge

activities.activity: Descend the south ridge and cross to the hut for a late meal
activities.notes: Tired-legs terrain — stay roped for the crevasse zones

activities.activity: Climb the Jungfrau normal route via the Rottalsattel (AD-)
activities.notes: 4,158 m — the Rottalsattel slope is the avalanche-prone crux; skip without regret if it's loaded

activities.activity: Train down to the valley for a celebration dinner

days.title: Buffer day
days.description: Weather insurance built into the plan

activities.activity: Spare day for a delayed objective, or sport climbing in the gorge
activities.notes: If everything already went to plan: via the Pfingstegg lift for an easy cragging day

days.title: Depart
days.description: Home with three summits in the bag

finalText:
With Mont Blanc and Gran Paradiso behind you, the Bernese Oberland trilogy above Grindelwald is exactly the right next step — and the Mittellegi ridge of the Eiger is the 'proper north-face-adjacent' line that's actually sensible for your level: D grade, hugely exposed, but on the crest rather than in the 1938 face itself (that's a different league and I won't pretend otherwise).

The plan builds logically: a warm-up ridge, a night at 3,657 m for acclimatisation, the Mönch as your first 4,000er of the trip, then the Eiger with a Jungfrau bonus if conditions allow. Day 9 is a deliberate buffer — in the Oberland you plan around the weather window, not the calendar, and the Mittellegi needs a dry ridge. Book an IFMGA guide (1:1 for the Eiger day is standard) and check the MeteoSwiss forecast and the hut's conditions reports in the final week; the Rottalsattel on the Jungfrau is the one slope with genuine avalanche risk in summer, so treat it as optional. Make sure your insurance covers helicopter rescue above 4,000 m in Switzerland.

Estimated cost for the two of you: £3,700 total — guide days shared where the ratio allows, hut half-board, lift and rail passes, and flights — comfortably inside your £4,000 budget. Want me to check flight options to Zurich for next July, or adjust the objectives?
